findings.where: Article specimen, body paragraphs, subhead and numbered list (desktop-04, desktop-05, desktop-06; phone-03, phone-04)
findings.fault: The article's running text and its numbered list are centred, while its title and byline sit flush left. Every line starts at a different point, so the eye has to hunt for each new line. In the list the numbers hang at the left and their text centres away from them: item 2's text starts well to the right of its number, so number and item barely read as a pair. On the phone this gives short centred lines in a ragged column.
findings.who_objects: A bank or agency reader reading one of Mark's long articles, which the brief calls the product. Centred prose tires them within a paragraph. Angélique, who will post every new article into this template, will find that each list and subhead she adds looks wrong.

findings.where: The blue band straight below the first screen: 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' with a white 'Subscribe' button (desktop-02 top, phone-01)
findings.fault: A second call to action sits right under the hero. Its full-width house-blue field and white button are louder than the hero's one action, 'Write to me directly'. Its serif heading is about as large as Mark's own line. It goes to #subscribe, and no subscribe form or section appears anywhere on the page, so the click goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one message and one quiet action, and for the first screen's contact to be the action. A visitor who clicks Subscribe lands nowhere and starts to doubt the site.

findings.where: The same band's heading, 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform'
findings.fault: The heading talks about Mark in the third person, straight after his first-person hero, so the page's voice switches to a marketer speaking for him. It also offers 'briefings', a newsletter the brief never mentions and Mark is not known to send. That is an invented offer.
findings.who_objects: The founder: the brief's personal-advisor test asks for Mark heard in the first person, and its copy rule says 'never invent claims'. Mark would be committed to a mailing he has not agreed to run.

findings.fault: There is no navigation. The top bar holds only the name and the logo: no links to articles, work, about or contact. The palette table still lists 'nav links' as a use of the mist colour, for links that do not exist.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first. The brief lists the nav first among its parts. A procurement reader who wants Mark's CV or his articles has nowhere to go.

findings.fault: The lectern photo is cropped to a huge head-and-shoulders. The hair is keyed out with a hard cut edge, so it reads as a cut-out pasted onto the navy, not as Mark speaking in a real room. The brief's 'Mark at work' becomes a portrait, and the lectern and the setting are gone.
findings.who_objects: The founder: v7's whole idea is 'a full-bleed photograph of Mark speaking', and the research asks for 'real people in real light'. A floating cut-out head looks cheap next to the refined serif.

findings.where: Section labels across the style tile: 'PALETTE' (desktop-02), 'Type pair', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch' (desktop-03, -04, -06), and 'Texture' (desktop-03)
findings.fault: Each label of the same kind is set differently. 'PALETTE' is in blue tracked capitals; three labels are small grey sans in sentence case; 'Texture' has no small label and instead gets a large italic serif heading used nowhere else. The type-pair note itself says 'Sentence case, never tracked capitals'.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the tile as a system: inconsistent labels make it look unfinished. Angélique gets no clear pattern to follow when she adds a section.

findings.where: Blue used on text a visitor cannot click: the 'PALETTE' label and the article list's numbers (desktop-02, desktop-05, phone-04)
findings.fault: House blue is the page's link colour, and the page itself says 'blue only where something can be clicked'. The label and the list numbers are static text in that same blue, so they look like links.
findings.who_objects: A reader who tries to click them and nothing happens. The page breaks its own stated rule, which weakens what blue means on the links that do work.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Streamlining the PPP Process' PDF card (desktop-06, phone-04)
findings.fault: This one card has a pale blue fill, a blue border, rounded corners and a wide soft drop shadow. Nothing else on the page is rounded or shadowed, and a hairline with a wide shadow on one resting element is the combination the house bans. It looks like an inserted promotion. Its download icon and 'PDF' label promise a file, but the link goes to #article on the same page.
findings.who_objects: A reader who expects the lecture PDF and gets a jump within the page. The founder, who asked for refined, not slick: the card is the one element that looks like a template widget.

findings.where: First screen and the band below it
findings.fault: Nothing near the action shows Mark's standing. There is no body that asked for his work, no region or year and no talk venue. The lede says whom he advises but gives no proof, and the space after the fold goes to the Subscribe band.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer deciding whether to write. They need to see that he has done this kind of work in their region before they email, and the first screen gives only a claim.

findings.where: First screen, the placeholder caption (desktop-01 bottom left; phone-01 below the action)
findings.fault: The caption saying the photo is a placeholder sits under the text column, far from the photograph. On the phone it sits below the action, a whole screen away from the image. It reads as a stray footnote about the heading, not as the photo's caption.
findings.who_objects: The founder or Mark, reading the tile, who may not link the note to the photograph it describes.

findings.where: Top bar, 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the logo (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The logo links home but the name next to it does not, though the two read as one lockup and the name leads. A visitor who clicks the name gets nothing.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects a site's name in the top-left to go home, as it does on most sites.

findings.fault: This is a button, but it is styled exactly like a text link (bold blue, underlined). The opening it replays is the hero at the top of the page, far out of view.
findings.who_objects: The founder reviewing the motion sketch, who clicks and may see nothing move where they are looking.

findings.where: Display type: 'The World's Best…' article title and 'Get Mark's briefings' (desktop-02, desktop-04)
findings.fault: The large serif lines use straight apostrophes, while the body text uses curly quotes (‘chapter topics’). At display size the straight mark is plain to see.
findings.who_objects: A typographically literate reader, and the founder judging the type pair, for whom this undercuts 'refined'.
